QUESTION: Can the file be read, and does it have a header and at least one data record?
COMMENT: 1,000 data records and 18 columns read (comma delimited, 1001 lines)
ACTION: Check the path and the format; a NONMEM dataset is a text file with a header line followed by one record per line.

QUESTION: Is the file free of a byte-order mark (BOM) at its start?
COMMENT: no byte-order mark
ACTION: Save the file as plain UTF-8 or ASCII without BOM; a BOM makes the first character of the header unreadable.

QUESTION: Is the file plain ASCII, without accented, typographic or other non-ASCII characters?
COMMENT: every character is ASCII
ACTION: Replace the characters (or remove them from comment columns); NONMEM reads ASCII only.

QUESTION: Are the line endings the same on every line (no mix of CRLF and LF, no lone CR)?
COMMENT: every line ends with LF
ACTION: Convert the file to one line-ending convention (LF for Linux/macOS NONMEM).

QUESTION: Is one field delimiter used throughout (not commas and tabs mixed)?
COMMENT: one delimiter (comma) throughout
ACTION: Re-export the dataset with a single delimiter, preferably commas.

QUESTION: Is the file free of blank lines between the records?
COMMENT: no blank lines
ACTION: Delete the blank lines; they can stop NM-TRAN or silently end the data.

QUESTION: Does every data record begin with a number (no comment lines, text lines or flagged records)?
COMMENT: every data record begins with a number
ACTION: Remove the lines, or make IGNORE= in $DATA match them; IGNORE=@ drops every record starting with a letter, silently.

QUESTION: Does every record have as many fields as the header has columns?
COMMENT: every record has 18 fields
ACTION: Fix the records with missing or extra delimiters; NM-TRAN reads fields by position.

QUESTION: Are there no trailing or doubled delimiters (empty extra fields)?
COMMENT: no line ends with a delimiter
ACTION: Remove the extra delimiter, or add a column name if the empty column is intended.

QUESTION: Are the data fields free of quotation marks?
COMMENT: no quotation marks
ACTION: Export the dataset without quoting; NM-TRAN cannot read quoted numbers.

QUESTION: Is every record shorter than the line-length limit?
COMMENT: longest line 76 characters (limit 1000)
ACTION: Drop unused columns or shorten the numbers; old NONMEM versions read 160 characters, NONMEM 7.3+ much more.

QUESTION: Does the last line end with a line terminator?
COMMENT: the file ends with a line terminator
ACTION: Add a final newline; some compilers drop an unterminated last record.

QUESTION: Are the required columns present (ID, TIME and DV by default)?
COMMENT: all 3 present: ID, TIME, DV
ACTION: Add or rename the column, or name it with --id-col, --time-col, --dv-col (or [data] in the settings file).

QUESTION: Are the recommended NONMEM columns present (AMT, EVID, MDV and CMT by default)?
COMMENT: all 4 present: AMT, EVID, MDV, CMT
ACTION: Add the columns; without EVID and MDV NONMEM infers them, which hides data errors.

QUESTION: Is the first line a header of names (not numbers), with no blank names?
COMMENT: the first line is a header of names
ACTION: Add or repair the header line; NM-TRAN needs the names for $INPUT, and a numeric first record would be data.

QUESTION: Are the column names unique, ignoring upper and lower case?
COMMENT: all column names are unique
ACTION: Rename the duplicates; $INPUT cannot hold two items with one name.

QUESTION: Are the column names valid NM-TRAN labels (letters, digits and underscore, beginning with a letter)?
COMMENT: every name is a valid NM-TRAN label
ACTION: Rename the columns; spaces, dots, hyphens and a leading digit are not allowed.

QUESTION: Is every column name within the length limit (20 characters)?
COMMENT: every name has at most 20 characters
ACTION: Shorten the names (the limit is SD in NONMEM's SIZES, 20 by default).

QUESTION: Are the column names free of NM-TRAN reserved words and abbreviated-code functions?
COMMENT: no column has a reserved name
ACTION: Rename the column (e.g. Y, T, A, F, R, D, EXP, LOG clash with NONMEM symbols), or DROP it in $INPUT.

QUESTION: Is the number of columns within the NM-TRAN limit (50 data items, DROP not counted)?
COMMENT: 18 columns (limit 50)
ACTION: Remove unused columns, or mark them =DROP in $INPUT; PD in SIZES sets the limit.

QUESTION: Are ID, TIME, DV, AMT, EVID, MDV, CMT, RATE, ADDL, II and SS numeric in every record?
COMMENT: every NONMEM data item is numeric
ACTION: Replace text by numbers (e.g. recode, convert clock times to hours); NM-TRAN stops at text in a data item it must read.

QUESTION: Are the other columns numeric, or text columns that you will DROP in $INPUT?
COMMENT: every other column is numeric
ACTION: Recode text covariates as numbers (SEX: 0/1), or write =DROP after them in $INPUT; list known text columns in [values] text_columns.

QUESTION: Are missing values written as blank or '.', and not as NA, NaN, NULL, N/A, - or similar?
COMMENT: no NA, NaN, NULL or similar markers
ACTION: Replace the markers by '.' (or by blank in a comma-delimited file).

QUESTION: Do the numbers use a decimal point (no decimal commas or thousands separators)?
COMMENT: no decimal commas
ACTION: Re-export with a decimal point and no thousands separators.

QUESTION: Do ID and TIME have a value in every record?
COMMENT: ID and TIME are filled in every record
ACTION: Fill in the missing values; NONMEM reads a blank as 0, which starts a new individual or a wrong time.

QUESTION: Are the numbers free of sentinel codes for 'missing' (-99, -999, ...)?
COMMENT: no sentinel codes
ACTION: Replace the code by '.' for a missing value (and decide how the covariate is imputed), or list it in [values] sentinels if it is genuine.

QUESTION: Are all numbers finite and of a magnitude NONMEM handles (not above 1e10)?
COMMENT: all values are finite and moderate
ACTION: Check the units and the scaling of the column.

QUESTION: Is every field at most 24 characters long (the NM-TRAN data item limit)?
COMMENT: no field is longer than 24 characters
ACTION: Round the numbers; NONMEM 7.1+ reads at most 24 characters in a data item.

QUESTION: Are the IDs whole numbers of at most 15 digits, and do different ID strings stay different as numbers?
COMMENT: IDs are whole numbers that stay distinct
ACTION: Renumber the individuals (keep the original in a column you DROP); NONMEM reads IDs as numbers, so 001 and 1 are one individual.

QUESTION: Is every column filled in at least once (no completely empty columns)?
COMMENT: no column is empty
ACTION: Remove the empty columns, or fill them.

QUESTION: Is EVID 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4 in every record?
COMMENT: EVID is one of 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 in every record
ACTION: Correct the event identifiers (0 observation, 1 dose, 2 other, 3 reset, 4 reset and dose).

QUESTION: Is MDV 0 or 1 in every record?
COMMENT: MDV is 0 or 1 in every record
ACTION: Correct the missing-dependent-variable flags.

QUESTION: Is MDV consistent with EVID (MDV = 1 on every record that is not an observation)?
COMMENT: MDV = 1 on every event record
ACTION: Set MDV = 1 on dose and other-event records; NONMEM rejects an event record with MDV = 0.

QUESTION: Does every observation record (EVID 0, MDV 0) have a DV?
COMMENT: every observation record has a DV
ACTION: Give the record a value, or set MDV = 1; a blank or '.' DV is read as 0 and is fitted as a measured zero.

QUESTION: Which observations are excluded on purpose (EVID 0 with MDV 1)?
COMMENT: no observation is excluded with MDV = 1
ACTION: Confirm that the exclusions are intended and documented; the DV of an excluded record is not used.

QUESTION: Do dose and other-event records have no DV (blank, '.' or 0)?
COMMENT: event records carry no DV
ACTION: Clear the DV of dose records; a stray value is ignored by NONMEM but misleads other tools.

QUESTION: Does every dose record (EVID 1 or 4) have a positive AMT?
COMMENT: every dose record has a positive AMT
ACTION: Give the dose its amount; a dose with AMT 0 or blank does nothing.

QUESTION: Are AMT and II non-negative, RATE 0 or above (or -1, -2), and ADDL a non-negative whole number?
COMMENT: no negative amounts, rates or intervals
ACTION: Correct the values; negative amounts and fractional codes are not valid NONMEM data.

QUESTION: Do observation records (EVID 0) have no dose amount?
COMMENT: observation records carry no dose amount
ACTION: Move the dose to its own record with EVID 1; NONMEM stops at an AMT on an observation record.

QUESTION: Is CMT a whole number within the range of compartments (|CMT| at most 99)?
COMMENT: CMT is a whole number in every record
ACTION: Correct the compartment numbers.

QUESTION: Which compartments receive the doses and which are observed, and is CMT given on every record when it is used?
COMMENT: doses into CMT 1 (100); observations in CMT 2 (900)
ACTION: Check that the doses and observations go to the compartments of your model.

QUESTION: Is RATE positive only on dose records with a positive AMT?
COMMENT: RATE appears on dose records with an amount only
ACTION: Remove the RATE from observation records, or add the missing AMT.

QUESTION: Are the infusion durations (AMT / RATE) within the limits you set?
COMMENT: no infusions (RATE > 0) in the data
ACTION: Check AMT and RATE units; set [events] min_infusion_duration and max_infusion_duration to the limits you expect.

QUESTION: Does ADDL > 0 come with II > 0, and is II > 0 used with ADDL or SS?
COMMENT: ADDL and II are used together
ACTION: Add the dosing interval II, or remove the unused II.

QUESTION: Are ADDL, II and SS used on dose records only?
COMMENT: ADDL, II and SS are used on dose records only
ACTION: Remove them from observation and other-event records.

QUESTION: Is SS one of 0, 1, 2, 3, and is SS > 0 on a dose record with II > 0?
COMMENT: no SS column
ACTION: Add II to the steady-state dose, or correct SS.

QUESTION: Are there no duplicated records (all fields identical; doses are checked by REC19)?
COMMENT: no record is duplicated
ACTION: Remove the duplicates unless a repeated dose or sample is intended.

QUESTION: Are there no two observations of one individual at one time and compartment with different DV?
COMMENT: no two observations share a time with different DV
ACTION: Decide which value is right (or whether the times differ); NONMEM would fit both at the same time.

QUESTION: Are there no two doses of one individual at one time and compartment (a double dose)?
COMMENT: no dose is recorded twice
ACTION: Remove the duplicate dose, or sum the amounts in one record.

QUESTION: Which reset and other-type events (EVID 2, 3, 4) are in the data?
COMMENT: no EVID 2, 3 or 4 records
ACTION: Check that the resets and other events are intended.

QUESTION: Is TIME non-decreasing within each individual (a lower time only on a reset record)?
COMMENT: TIME never decreases within an individual
ACTION: Sort the records by ID and time, or correct the time; NONMEM stops when TIME decreases.

QUESTION: Are the records of each ID together in one block (no ID reappears after another)?
COMMENT: every ID is one block (100 individuals)
ACTION: Sort by ID; NONMEM treats every block as a separate individual, so a split ID is two individuals.

QUESTION: Is TIME free of negative values?
COMMENT: no negative times
ACTION: Negative times are allowed for pre-dose samples, but check that they are intended.

QUESTION: Is the largest TIME plausible for the time unit (below the limit you set)?
COMMENT: the largest TIME is 24 (limit 1.00e5)
ACTION: A huge TIME suggests dates, seconds or clock times; convert to hours (or your unit) since the first dose.

QUESTION: Which observations share a time with a dose of the same individual, and do they come before or after the dose?
COMMENT: no observation shares a time with a dose
ACTION: In NONMEM the order of the records decides: a pre-dose sample must be written before the dose record.

QUESTION: Is the time between consecutive records of an individual below the gap limit you set?
COMMENT: no gap limit set ([time] max_gap)
ACTION: Check for missing records or a wrong time unit. The check runs when [time] max_gap is set.

QUESTION: Does the TAD column equal the time since the latest dose?
COMMENT: no TAD column named (--tad-col)
ACTION: Recompute TAD, or check the dose records. The check runs when a TAD column is named.

QUESTION: Is the actual TIME close to the nominal time?
COMMENT: no nominal-time column named (--nominal-time-col)
ACTION: Check the sampling times against the schedule. The check runs when a nominal-time column is named.

QUESTION: Which observations come before the first dose of the individual?
COMMENT: no observation precedes the first dose
ACTION: Confirm that pre-dose and baseline samples are intended.

QUESTION: Does every individual with observations have at least one dose record?
COMMENT: every individual with observations has a dose
ACTION: Add the dose records. For data without doses (baseline, PD only) set [dosing] require_dose = false.

QUESTION: Does every individual with a dose have at least one observation?
COMMENT: every dosed individual has observations
ACTION: Individuals without observations add nothing to the estimation; remove them or add the observations.

QUESTION: Is the first dose of each individual at TIME 0?
COMMENT: every first dose is at time 0
ACTION: Make TIME the time since the first dose; if not, set [time] first_dose_at_zero = false.

QUESTION: Does the dose amount stay the same within each individual?
COMMENT: each individual keeps one dose amount
ACTION: Dose changes are fine when intended (titration); check the individuals listed.

QUESTION: Are all dose amounts near the usual dose levels (no unit slips of 10 times or more)?
COMMENT: 2 dose levels, none an outlier (median dose 75)
ACTION: Check the units of AMT of the individuals listed (mg or g, per kg or total).

QUESTION: Are the dosing intervals regular within each individual?
COMMENT: no individual has three or more dose records
ACTION: Irregular intervals are fine when intended; check the individuals listed.

QUESTION: What are the dose levels, routes (compartments) and regimens?
COMMENT: 100 dose records in 100 individuals; 2 dose level(s): 50 (50), 100 (50); into CMT 1 (100)
ACTION: Compare the summary with the protocol.

QUESTION: Does the dataset have observation records?
COMMENT: 900 observation records, 900 of them used (MDV 0)
ACTION: A dataset without observations cannot be fitted.

QUESTION: Is DV free of negative values?
COMMENT: no negative DV
ACTION: A negative concentration is impossible; for data that can be negative (PD, change from baseline) set [observations] negative_ok = true.

QUESTION: Are the DV values of 0 explained (before the first dose or flagged as BLQ)?
COMMENT: no DV of 0
ACTION: Flag them as BLQ or set MDV = 1; a DV of 0 cannot be log-transformed. Set [observations] zero_ok = true if zeros are genuine.

QUESTION: Are BLQ observations handled consistently (flag agrees with the LLOQ, one imputation rule)?
COMMENT: no BLQ flag column ([columns] blq), LLOQ (--lloq) or LLOQ column to check against
ACTION: Use one rule for all BLQ samples (flag them, give them one DV, or set MDV = 1).

QUESTION: Is the fraction of BLQ observations below the limit you set?
COMMENT: no BLQ flag, LLOQ or LLOQ column
ACTION: With many BLQ observations, use a likelihood-based method (M3/M4) rather than imputation.

QUESTION: Are there concentrations far from those of other individuals at similar times after the dose?
COMMENT: 2 outlying concentration(s) (2 individuals). For example: line 381 ID 38: DV = 0.0011 is 196.7x below the typical value per unit dose at about 24 h after the dose (24–24); line 961 ID 96: DV = 0.0127 is 32.663x below the typical value per unit dose at about 24 h after the dose (24–24)
ACTION: Check the listed values against the source data; remove or exclude (MDV = 1) only with a documented reason.

QUESTION: Are there isolated spikes within an individual's profile (a value far above both neighbours after the peak)?
COMMENT: no spikes within the profiles
ACTION: Check the sample times and the values against the source data.

QUESTION: Are the concentrations before the first dose zero or below the quantification limit?
COMMENT: no pre-dose samples
ACTION: Check for carry-over, wrong times or mislabelled doses; set [observations] predose_tolerance for endogenous compounds.

QUESTION: Does every individual have at least the minimum number of observations?
COMMENT: every individual with observations has at least 2
ACTION: Individuals with a single observation add little; check whether records are missing.

QUESTION: Does every individual have at least one quantifiable concentration after the first dose?
COMMENT: every dosed individual has a quantifiable post-dose concentration
ACTION: Individuals with no quantifiable concentration are uninformative for the structural model.

QUESTION: Is the scale of DV as declared (natural concentrations or their logarithm)?
COMMENT: DV runs from 0.0011 to 4.293 (median 0.9488), as expected for concentrations
ACTION: Check --dv-log: DV must be ln(concentration) when it is given as the logarithm.

QUESTION: Which observation types are present (DVID or compartment) and how many records has each?
COMMENT: compartments of the observations (CMT): 2 (900)
ACTION: Check that each type has its own identifier and that the model handles each.

QUESTION: What is the sampling design (observations per individual and times after the dose)?
COMMENT: 900 used observations in 100 individuals; per individual: minimum 9, median 9, maximum 9; time after the dose 0.5 to 24 with 9 distinct sampling times
ACTION: Compare the design with the protocol.

QUESTION: How many individuals, records, doses and observations does the dataset have?
COMMENT: 100 individuals, 1,000 records (blocks of one ID: 100), 100 doses and 900 observations used (plus 0 with MDV 1); records per individual: minimum 10, median 10, maximum 10
ACTION: Compare the counts with the source.

QUESTION: Does every individual have more than one record?
COMMENT: every individual has at least 2 records
ACTION: An individual with a single record cannot contribute; check whether records were lost.

QUESTION: Do the grouping columns stay constant within each individual?
COMMENT: no grouping column named (--group or [data] group), or all are listed as time-varying
ACTION: Correct the labels, or list the column in [subjects] time_varying_groups when it changes by period.

QUESTION: Is the number of records per individual free of extreme values?
COMMENT: record counts are close to the median of 10
ACTION: Check the individuals with very many or very few records for duplicated or missing blocks.

QUESTION: Does every individual have at least one observation that is used (MDV 0)?
COMMENT: every individual has an observation that is used
ACTION: An individual whose observations are all excluded adds nothing.

QUESTION: Does every individual start with a dose or event record (not an observation)?
COMMENT: every individual starts with a dose or an event record
ACTION: A first record that is an observation is fine for baseline samples; check the individuals listed.

QUESTION: Which covariates were examined, and are they continuous, categorical or time-varying?
COMMENT: 8 covariates — continuous: WT, AGE, EGFR, CRCL; categorical: GROUP (2 levels), DOSE (2 levels), SEX (2 levels), BLQ (1 levels)
ACTION: Name the covariates yourself with [covariates] columns, categorical and time_varying if the detection is wrong.

QUESTION: Are the covariates free of missing values (blank, '.' or a sentinel code)?
COMMENT: no missing covariate values in 8 covariates
ACTION: Impute or fill in the values; NONMEM reads a blank or '.' as 0, which silently becomes a value of the covariate.

QUESTION: Are the covariate values within plausible ranges?
COMMENT: WT, AGE within the ranges ([covariates.ranges])
ACTION: Check the listed values against the source; set the ranges in [covariates.ranges].

QUESTION: Are the baseline covariates constant within each individual?
COMMENT: 8 baseline covariates are constant within every individual
ACTION: Correct the values, or list the covariate in [covariates] time_varying if it changes.

QUESTION: Do the categorical covariates have the expected levels, none of them rare?
COMMENT: GROUP (2 levels), DOSE (2 levels), SEX (2 levels), BLQ (1 levels)
ACTION: Recode or merge rare levels; declare the levels in [covariates.levels].

QUESTION: Are the continuous covariates free of extreme values (beyond the Tukey fences)?
COMMENT: 4 continuous covariates without extreme values
ACTION: Check the listed individuals against the source data.

QUESTION: Is every covariate variable (more than one value)?
COMMENT: 1 constant covariate(s) (1 individual). For example: line 2 ID 1: BLQ has the single value 0
ACTION: A constant covariate carries no information and can be dropped from the analysis.

QUESTION: Are the continuous covariates free of strong pairwise correlation (|r| below the limit)?
COMMENT: 2 strongly associated covariate pair(s) (1 individual). For example: line 2 ID 1: EGFR and CRCL: r = 0.98 (100 individuals); line 2 ID 1: GROUP and DOSE: Cramér's V = 1.00 (100 individuals)
ACTION: Strongly correlated covariates cannot be told apart in a covariate model; choose one or a composite.

QUESTION: Are derived covariates consistent with their parts (BMI and BSA from weight and height)?
COMMENT: needs BMI or BSA together with weight (WT) and height (HT)
ACTION: Recompute the derived covariate, or check the units of weight and height.

QUESTION: Do the magnitudes of AGE, WT and HT suggest the usual units (years, kg, cm)?
COMMENT: AGE, WT and HT magnitudes agree with years, kg and cm
ACTION: Convert the unit (e.g. HT in m to cm, AGE in days to years).

QUESTION: Do time-varying covariates change plausibly between consecutive records?
COMMENT: no time-varying continuous covariate
ACTION: Check the listed jumps; a weight that changes by half between visits is usually an error.

QUESTION: Will the IGNORE option you plan to use skip the header line and nothing else?
COMMENT: IGNORE=@ skips the header (line 1)
ACTION: Use $DATA ... IGNORE=@ for a header that starts with a letter; the default IGNORE=# would read the header as data.

QUESTION: Which $DATA and $INPUT statements fit this file?
COMMENT: $DATA analysis.csv IGNORE=@; $INPUT with 18 of 18 columns (the rest as =DROP); the full statements are in qc_nonmem.txt
ACTION: Copy them from qc_nonmem.txt into the control stream and adjust.

QUESTION: Which special data items are used, and what do they require of the model?
COMMENT: no special data items (RATE, ADDL, II, SS, EVID 2–4) are used
ACTION: Make sure the model defines what the data items need (R1/D1 for RATE -1/-2, PREDPP for ADDL, II and SS).
